references.text: Jacob's blessing of Judah prophesies that the scepter shall not depart from Judah until Shiloh (the Messiah) comes – a messianic prophecy written by Moses in the Law, as Philip refers to in [ref:1 Mos 49:10|Genesis 49:10].
Moses wrote in the Law about the coming prophet like himself whom God would raise up. Philip claims that Jesus is the fulfillment of this promise, cf. [ref:5 Mos 18:15-18|Deuteronomy 18:15-18].

The prophet Isaiah prophesied about the virgin birth and Immanuel – one of the prophecies Philip may have had in mind when he said "the one whom the prophets wrote about," cf. [ref:Jes 7:14|Isaiah 7:14].

Isaiah's prophecy about the child who is born and the son who is given, with dominion on his shoulder, is a central messianic prophecy that Philip may have referred to, see [ref:Jes 9:6-7|Isaiah 9:6-7].

Isaiah's song of the suffering servant is among the most central messianic prophecies that Philip likely had in mind when he said that the prophets wrote about Jesus, see [ref:Jes 53:1-12|Isaiah 53:1-12].
Matthew links Jesus' upbringing in Nazareth to the prophecy that he would be called a Nazarene, confirming Philip's description of Jesus as "from Nazareth," cf. [ref:Matt 2:23|Matthew 2:23].
Luke confirms that Jesus was held to be the son of Joseph, which directly corresponds with Philip's description of him as "Jesus, son of Joseph, from Nazareth," see [ref:Luk 3:23|Luke 3:23].
The risen Jesus himself explained to the disciples what had been written about him in Moses and all the prophets – the same reference Philip used toward Nathanael, see [ref:Luk 24:27|Luke 24:27].

Jesus said that everything written about him in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms must be fulfilled – this supports Philip's claim that Moses and the prophets wrote about Jesus, cf. [ref:Luk 24:44|Luke 24:44].
Just before this, Andrew finds his brother Simon and tells him they have found the Messiah. Philip's testimony to Nathanael parallels Andrew's testimony, see [ref:Joh 1:41-42|John 1:41-42].
Jesus himself confirms what Philip said, namely that Moses wrote about him. In [ref:Joh 5:46|John 5:46] Jesus says: "If you believed Moses, you would believe me, for he wrote about me."
Paul testifies that he says nothing other than what Moses and the prophets said should happen – that the Messiah must suffer and rise again, cf. [ref:Apg 26:22-23|Acts 26:22-23].
